top_strength: He was honest and quick with a hard number, and handled the customer's self-conscious moments well — 'welcome to Austin', 'I'm sorry to hear that', and 'no, you're good' when she apologized for a question.
coaching_note: He steered a live, ready-to-buy lead to a competitor (Dolly.com) twice — before he had the zip codes, and again after quoting — without ever selling a single Einstein differentiator. Even when the minimum genuinely doesn't pencil for a two-item job, quote the value first ($2,000 No Worries, on-time guarantee, no deposit, fully insured crew) and let the customer decide; a 21-year-old with no help and a third-floor apartment is exactly who buys peace of mind.
phone_presence_notes: Polite but transactional and low-energy — never used her name, met her joke ('try not to spend $1 million') with 'Mm-hmm. Okay.', and left her audibly deflated at 'Goodness gracious' without any recovery attempt.
audio_review_reason: Presence scored 2 — verify from audio whether the delivery was genuinely flat/disinterested or whether the transcript is understating warmth in the Dolly.com referral.
